title: PATS and Keyless Entry Component Locations
introduction:
The passive anti-theft system (PATS) map is easier to read when I treat it as a map of several locations around the car, rather than a treasure hunt for a single anti-theft box. Follow the leader lines between the transparent vehicle and the enlarged components, then match the callouts to the table.

The drawing places the BCM toward the front of the cabin, the PATS center antenna in the center-console area and the keyless entry rear antenna at the rear of the vehicle. It also identifies antennas within the exterior front door handles. The handle illustration represents those antenna locations, not a separate loose antenna mounted beside the handle.

RTM means radio transceiver module. Select its coupe or convertible entry before using the location shown; the map includes both configurations. Keep that body-style choice alongside the table rather than assuming every illustrated module belongs in the same car.

The cupholder inset identifies the passive key backup starting location, with the key shown in the cupholder area beneath the raised cover. I use that inset as a landmark, not as a complete backup-starting instruction. This reference supplies component locations, not key-placement orientation, the starting sequence, trim access, programming or electrical tests. Those actions need their matching instructions after the relevant location has been identified.
